quantityPriceSnapshot.createDescription: Enter the month-end quantity and price per unit. The total value is derived ({{currency}}).
quantityPriceSnapshot.editDescription: Update the quantity, price, statement date, or note. To change the month, delete and re-create.

accruedInterestSnapshot.createDescription: Enter the month-end total value and the accrued interest component ({{currency}}). Total already includes accrued.
accruedInterestSnapshot.editDescription: Update the total value, accrued, statement date, or note. To change the month, delete and re-create.
accruedInterestSnapshot.createDescriptionTimeDeposit: Enter the month-end value from your bank statement ({{currency}}). The interest is worked out for you.
accruedInterestSnapshot.editDescriptionTimeDeposit: Update the value, statement date, or note. The interest is worked out for you. To change the month, delete and re-create.
accruedInterestSnapshot.accruedHint: Leave accrued at 0 if your bond pays coupons directly to your bank account each period (government retail bonds like ORI and SBR). Enter an amount for bonds bought from another investor and for time deposits, where the interest is kept inside the investment.
accruedInterestSnapshot.accruedHintAccrues: This bond keeps its coupons inside the bond, so enter the accrued interest included in this month's total value — read it from your statement.

trade.buyDescription: Quantity acquired and the price paid per unit. Total cash out is derived ({{currency}}).
trade.sellDescription: Quantity sold and the price received per unit. Total cash in is derived ({{currency}}).
trade.separateNote: This records the trade. Update the holding in this month's snapshot, and the bank balance in that account.
trade.editDescription: Adjust the trade date, quantity, price, or note.

cashIncome.createDescription: Cash payment received from the instrument. This will not update any bank balance — the cash appears in the next bank statement.
cashIncome.editDescription: Adjust the payment date, amount, or note.

fee.createDescription: Manager-imposed fee. Set quantity + price only when the manager settles by removing units (e.g., gold storage fees). Fees already built into a mutual fund's price per unit are in the snapshot — don't record them here.
fee.editDescription: Adjust the fee date, amount, deducted units, or note.
fee.incompleteHint: If recording a unit-settled fee, fill in both quantity and price.
fee.derivedHint: Auto-filled from cash ÷ price. Edit to override.

maturityTxn.createDescription: This investment reached its scheduled end. Record the principal, the interest, and what happened to each. A rolled portion becomes a new investment — create it separately if needed.
maturityTxn.editDescription: Adjust the principal, interest, what happened to each, or the note.

headline.unrealizedPLHint: On paper: what you'd gain or lose if you sold at this month's price.

stock.listSubtitle: Listed equities — tracked by ticker and exchange, with monthly quantity-and-price snapshots.
stock.emptyBody: Create your first stock to start tracking month-end quantity and price.
stock.createDescription: Track a listed equity. Monthly snapshots record quantity and price per unit; the total value derives from those.
stock.editDescription: Currency can't be changed. To use a different one, create a new stock. Ownership can be changed.
stock.snapshotsDescription: Monthly quantity and price readings (manual entry).
stock.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshots yet. A snapshot is the value on your statement at month-end. Record one each month.
stock.transactionsEmpty: No transactions yet. Record a Buy or Dividend to start the ledger.
stock.reconcileWarning: Latest snapshot quantity ({{actual}} sh) doesn't match ledger total ({{expected}} sh). Snapshots remain the source of truth — review trades or fees if this is unexpected.

tour.overviewBody: Everything about one stock holding — its current value, what you paid, and every trade and dividend.
tour.headlineBody: “Total cost” is tallied from your Buy and Sell transactions. Gain or loss compares it to the latest recorded value.
tour.actionsBody: Use “Edit” to change its details, “Close…” to mark it ended — it then stops counting toward your net worth — or “Delete” to remove it entirely.
tour.detailsBody: The ticker and basics were set when you added the stock. Use “Edit” to change them.
tour.chartBody: The shaded area is the recorded value each month; the line beneath is your cost. The gap between them is your gain.
tour.snapshotsBody: Each row records a month's share count and price. Tap “Record snapshot” to add this month's value (shares × price), or “Import” to add several at once.
tour.transactionsBody: Record every Buy and Sell — they drive your cost basis — plus dividends received and any fees.

mutualFund.snapshotsDescription: Monthly units and price per unit — the NAV your fund manager publishes (manual entry).
mutualFund.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshots yet. A snapshot is the value on your statement at month-end. Record one each month.
mutualFund.transactionsEmpty: No transactions yet. Record a Buy or Distribution to start the ledger.
mutualFund.reconcileWarning: Latest snapshot units ({{actual}}) don't match ledger total ({{expected}}). Snapshots remain the source of truth — review trades or fees if this is unexpected.

tour.detailsBody: The fund's basics were set when you added it. Use “Edit” to change them.
tour.chartBody: The shaded area is the recorded value each month; the line beneath is your cost. The gap between them is your gain.

bond.listSubtitle: Fixed-income instruments — tracked by series, issuer, coupon, and maturity, with monthly accrued-interest snapshots.
bond.emptyBody: Create your first bond to start tracking month-end value and accrued interest.
bond.createDescription: Track a fixed-income instrument by face value, coupon, and maturity. Monthly snapshots record the total value and the accrued-interest part.
bond.editDescription: Currency can't be changed. To use a different one, create a new bond. Ownership can be changed.
bond.snapshotsDescription: Monthly total value and accrued-interest breakdown.
bond.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshots yet. A snapshot is the value on your statement at month-end. Record one each month. For a bond held to maturity (government retail bonds that pay coupons to your bank), one starting snapshot at face value is enough — it carries forward each month until maturity.
bond.transactionsDescription: Buys and sells (from another investor), coupons, fees, and the maturity. For government retail bonds like ORI and SBR, log each coupon as received.
bond.transactionsEmpty: No transactions yet. Record a Buy or Coupon to start the ledger.
bond.secondaryBuyHint: A bond bought from another investor is entered by recording the actual purchase as a Buy transaction after creating — that captures your real price (discount or premium).

couponDisposition.hint: Where do the coupons go? “Paid to my bank” means each coupon lands in your bank account (most government retail bonds). “Kept in the bond” means it builds up inside the bond — pick this and the monthly snapshot form will ask for the accrued interest.

placeholders.faceValue: e.g. 50,000,000 for 50 lots of IDR 1,000,000 each

tour.overviewBody: This page holds everything about one bond — what it's worth now, what you paid for it, and every payment it makes along the way.
tour.headlineBody: “Total cost” is what the bond cost you. For a government bond bought at issue that's its face value; once you record Buy and Sell transactions, it's tallied from those instead. Gain or loss is the latest recorded value minus that cost.
tour.actionsBody: Use “Edit” to change its details, “Close…” to mark it ended — it then stops counting toward your net worth — or “Delete” to remove it entirely.
tour.detailsBody: Face value, coupon rate, and maturity date were set when you added the bond. Use “Edit” to change any of them.
tour.chartBody: The shaded area is the bond's recorded value each month; the line beneath is your cost. When the line sits below the area, the gap is your gain — your gain or loss over time.
tour.snapshotsBody: Each row is one month's recorded value. Tap “Record snapshot” to add what the bond is worth this month, or “Import” for several months — and when the bond matures, the closing one is added for you automatically.
tour.transactionsBody: Log the coupons you receive and any fees — the totals above tally your income to date. Record extra Buys or Sells if you buy or sell from another investor. When the bond matures, post a Maturity entry: it records the final payout, files the closing snapshot automatically, and marks the bond closed. The payout lands in your bank, not here, so for an accurate month update your bank balance for that month too — at month-end, record every investment's value and your bank balances together.

timeDeposit.listSubtitle: Locked-principal bank placements — tracked by bank, rate, and term, with monthly accrued-interest snapshots.
timeDeposit.emptyBody: Create your first time deposit to start tracking month-end value and accrued interest.
timeDeposit.createDescription: Track a locked principal at a bank — fixed rate, fixed term. Monthly snapshots record the total value and the accrued-interest breakdown.
timeDeposit.editDescription: Currency can't be changed. To use a different one, create a new time deposit. Ownership can be changed.
timeDeposit.subtitle: {{bank}} · {{rate}}% · {{months}}mo
timeDeposit.snapshotsDescription: Monthly total value and accrued-interest breakdown.
timeDeposit.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshots yet. A snapshot is the value on your statement at month-end. Record one each month.
timeDeposit.transactionsDescription: Record the Maturity when the term ends. These start from what you said happens at maturity. Change them if the bank did something else.
timeDeposit.transactionsEmpty: No transactions yet. Record a Maturity when the term ends.
timeDeposit.rolloverHint: What the bank does automatically at maturity if you take no action. Auto-renew with interest = compound; auto-renew principal = interest paid out, principal rolls; no rollover = bank releases everything to your account.
timeDeposit.maturityAfterPlacement: Maturity date must be after the placement date.

rollover.calloutTitle: This deposit matured and rolled over.
rollover.calloutBody: {{amount}} is being reinvested. Create the new deposit to keep tracking it.
rollover.linkDescription: Pick the deposit you already created for the rolled-over funds. We'll connect them so this notice goes away.
rollover.linkEmpty: No eligible deposits to link. Create one first, or it may already be linked elsewhere.

rolloverChain.title: Rollover
rolloverChain.description: How this deposit connects to the ones before and after it.

tour.overviewTitle: Your time deposit at a glance
tour.overviewBody: Everything about one deposit — its value, the principal you placed, and its maturity.
tour.headlineBody: “Total cost” is the principal you placed. Gain or loss is the latest recorded value — principal plus interest earned — minus that.
tour.actionsBody: Use “Edit” to change its details, “Close…” to mark it ended — it then stops counting toward your net worth — or “Delete” to remove it entirely.
tour.detailsBody: Principal, interest rate, and maturity date were set when you opened the deposit. Use “Edit” to change them.
tour.chartBody: The shaded area is the recorded value each month; the line beneath is your principal. The gap between them is the interest earned.
tour.snapshotsBody: Each row records a month's value — principal plus interest accrued so far. Tap “Record snapshot” to add this month's, or “Import” for several months.
tour.transactionsBody: A time deposit has one transaction: when it matures, post a Maturity entry for the payout, and choose whether to cash it out or roll it into a new deposit. If you cash out, the money lands in your bank, not here — update your bank balance for that month so your net worth stays accurate. At month-end, record every investment's value and your bank balances together.

gold.listSubtitle: Physical or digital gold tracked by form and purity. Snapshots record month-end grams held and price per gram.
gold.emptyBody: Create your first gold to start tracking month-end grams and price.
gold.createDescription: Track physical or digital gold. Monthly snapshots record grams held and price per gram; the total value derives from those.
gold.editDescription: Currency can't be changed. To use a different one, create a new gold. Ownership can be changed.
gold.snapshotsDescription: Monthly grams and price-per-gram readings (manual entry).
gold.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshots yet. A snapshot is the value on your statement at month-end. Record one each month.
gold.transactionsDescription: Trades and fees. Storage / unit-deduction fees affect the next snapshot's quantity.
gold.transactionsEmpty: No transactions yet. Record a Buy to start the ledger.
gold.reconcileWarning: Latest snapshot grams ({{actual}} g) don't match ledger total ({{expected}} g). Snapshots remain the source of truth — review trades or fees if this is unexpected.
gold.snapshotPriceHint: Use the buyback price — what a dealer would pay you today, not the higher selling price. This keeps your net worth at what the gold could actually be cashed out for.
gold.buyPriceHint: The dealer's selling price — what you paid per gram (higher than the buyback).
gold.sellPriceHint: The buyback price — what the dealer actually paid you per gram.

tour.overviewBody: Everything about one gold holding — its value, what you paid, and every buy and sell.
tour.headlineBody: “Total cost” is tallied from your Buy and Sell transactions. Gain or loss compares it to the latest recorded value.
tour.actionsBody: Use “Edit” to change its details, “Close…” to mark it ended — it then stops counting toward your net worth — or “Delete” to remove it entirely.
tour.detailsBody: Weight and purity were set when you added the gold. Use “Edit” to change them.
tour.chartBody: The shaded area is the recorded value each month; the line beneath is your cost. The gap between them is your gain.
tour.snapshotsBody: Each row records a month's weight and price. Tap “Record snapshot” to add this month's value (weight × price), or “Import” to add several at once. Use the buyback price — what a dealer would pay you — so the value reflects what you could cash out for today.
tour.transactionsBody: Record every Buy and Sell, plus any fees — they drive your cost basis. Gold has no dividends or coupons.
